releases.notes:
RigTune 0.5.1 for Minecraft Java 26.2 and 26.3 (Fabric). Download the jar for your Minecraft version: `rigtune-0.5.1+mc26.2.jar` or `rigtune-0.5.1+mc26.3.jar` (the `-sources` jars are the source code). It needs Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer and Fabric API.

## Fixes

- **Modrinth App repair steps that work in the app as it is now (0.21.6).** For each old copy an older RigTune left:
  - if it's listed in Content, switched off, delete it there;
  - if it isn't, delete RigTune's newer copy, rename the old one from `.jar.disabled` to `.jar`, press Refresh, then Update.

  The notice's title now fits ("Fix the Modrinth App's mod list"), and **Copy steps** copies the steps with the file names. RigTune 0.1-0.4 get the same steps in their launcher warning (rules revision 18).
- **Intel Arc 130T and 140T** laptop graphics are recognised as integrated: GPU tier 3 instead of 2, plus the integrated-GPU advice. Integrated GPUs show "shared memory" instead of a misleading VRAM figure (rules revision 19).
- "RigTune applied N change(s)" counts an update once (2 updates read "4 changes").
- Your first Apply no longer counts the game's own switch of Preset to Custom as one of your settings.
- The "RigTune uses the network" toast no longer shows over the benchmark results.

No file format changed: every file 0.1.0 to 0.5.0 wrote keeps working. This was checked with the released jars: self-updates from 0.1.0 to 0.4.0, downgrades to 0.4.0 and 0.3.0, and undo after a restart, on 26.2 and 26.3. The rules update to revision 19.

**Full changelog**: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#051---2026-09-29) · [compare v0.5.0...v0.5.1](https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/compare/v0.5.0...v0.5.1)

releases.notes:
RigTune 0.5.0 for Minecraft Java 26.2 and 26.3 (Fabric). Download the jar for your Minecraft version: `rigtune-0.5.0+mc26.2.jar` or `rigtune-0.5.0+mc26.3.jar` (the `-sources` jars are the source code). It needs Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer and Fabric API.

## Highlights

- **RigTune never fights your launcher.** Some launchers keep their own list of an instance's mods: the Modrinth App, the CurseForge app, ATLauncher, GDLauncher, and Prism Launcher or PolyMC once they've installed mods. There, mod installs, updates and disables become advice with that launcher's own steps. Settings still apply in one click.
  - Instances an older RigTune already changed get a repair notice.
  - **Settings → Mod files** brings 0.4's behaviour back for one instance.
- **Try it (measured)**: tick one setting in Preview, and RigTune measures your game before and after the change, in the same place, and shows how the 1 % lows and the average moved.
- **Stutter Doctor one-click fixes** for Sodium's Chunk Updates, render distance and Distant Horizons' thread count. A fix is offered only when a monitor session backs it, and it is compared against a fresh session afterwards.
- **Profiles for servers**: RigTune can offer a profile you picked when you join a server, a LAN game or a Realm. It never switches on its own.
- **First-time Apply guide** for new players, and **launch-time alerts** when a launch is noticeably slower than your usual.
- **Settings changed outside the game** (for example by a launcher's settings sync) are listed, with a one-click way to apply RigTune's values again.
- Many fixes, including:
  - RigTune no longer claims mod files it didn't put there;
  - Undo no longer guesses `.disabled` files;
  - pending changes that can never run are dropped;
  - the benchmark and the Stutter Doctor give steadier results.

No file format changed. Every file 0.1.0 to 0.4.0 wrote keeps working, and a downgrade to 0.4.0 keeps working too. This was checked with the released jars: self-updates from 0.1.0 to 0.4.0 on 26.2 and 26.3, downgrades to 0.4.0 and 0.3.0, and undo after a restart. The rules update to revision 17.

**Full changelog**: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#050---2026-09-28) (including known issues) · [compare v0.4.0...v0.5.0](https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0)

releases.notes:
RigTune 0.4.0 for Minecraft Java 26.2 and 26.3 (Fabric). Download the jar for your Minecraft version: `rigtune-0.4.0+mc26.2.jar` or `rigtune-0.4.0+mc26.3.jar` (the `-sources` jars are the source code). It needs Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer and Fabric API.

## Highlights

- **Tools…** on the RigTune screen opens the new tools. All of them work with the network off and send nothing anywhere.
- **Performance Profiles and share codes**: switch your video, Sodium, Distant Horizons and Iris settings between Max FPS, Balanced, Quality, Battery, Recording, your own settings and saved or imported profiles in one click. A switch is an ordinary Apply, so History shows it and Undo works. A share code (about 100 characters) holds only setting values, and importing one always shows a Preview first.
- **Stutter Doctor**: an opt-in session monitor (off by default) that shows where the time went when the game hitches (garbage collection, chunk loading and building, game ticks, or "not explained") and what may help.
- **JVM & memory**: the Java your game runs on, and notes on Java arguments that Java ignores or that only cost memory, with your launcher's steps. It never suggests adding garbage-collector flags; your Java arguments are never shown, logged or shared.
- **Benchmark history and regression alerts**: runs are compared only under the same conditions; a drop in 1% lows beyond the run-to-run noise is flagged, with the changes since then listed as "may be related".
- **Notices** for a server's view-distance limit, a GPU or driver change, new recommendations after a rules update, and a benchmark that needs a rerun.
- **Estimated tier** instead of "limited by"; **VSync off** is optional and says what it does; MultiMC and GDLauncher are recognised.
- **Keyboard and Narrator** support for every list row, and high-contrast colours.
- **Fixes that also affect 0.3.0**: clicking a row in History on 26.3; a second "Undo last" skipping a staged setting; updates now respect other mods' version requirements; a helper killed mid-update is finished or rolled back at the next run; undo keeps a mod and its library together; "Undo all" still reaches your original settings after a long history.

No file format changed: every file 0.1.0 to 0.3.0 wrote keeps working, and 0.3.0 reads what 0.4.0 writes (checked with the released jars, including self-updates from 0.1.0, 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 and a downgrade to 0.3.0 and back).

**Full changelog**: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-09-26) · [compare v0.3.0...v0.4.0](https://github.com/chaotix345/rigtune/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0)
